title: A write needs a second look
goal: {{mark}} wants to change one setting on a tenant that {{vocab.org}} runs, through the hosted MCP server, without risking a wrong write.
obstacle: An admin-plane MCP tool can change or delete real tenant objects. A typed call that looks right can still carry the wrong argument.
control: Writes are off by default. When they are on, each call shows the exact arguments and a hash of them, and a destructive call also needs the tool name typed.

steps.title: Writes are off
steps.tell: Call a write tool with writes off. The call is refused before it leaves this app, and the refusal is in the audit log.
steps.say: By default this tool can look and not touch.
steps.why: A read-only default turns a wrong click into a harmless one.

blocked.tell: The call is refused with a message that names the setting to change. Nothing was sent to the server.

steps.title: Turn writes on for this connection
steps.tell: {{mark}} turns on allow writes for one connection. A red banner stays visible while it is on.
steps.say: Writes are a decision for this connection, and the page says so.
steps.why: The banner keeps the state visible for everyone who looks at the screen.

steps.title: Review the exact arguments
steps.tell: Press Call. A dialog shows the exact arguments and their hash. Changing an argument after review changes the hash and the call is refused.
steps.say: What I approve is exactly what runs.
steps.why: The hash binds the approval to the arguments, so a swapped argument cannot ride on an earlier approval.

blocked.tell: If the arguments change after the review the hash no longer matches and the server of this app refuses the call.
blocked.say: The approval does not carry over to different arguments.

steps.title: Type the name for a destructive call
steps.tell: A delete asks {{mark}} to type the tool name. Only then does the confirm button work.
steps.say: A delete costs a few extra keystrokes on purpose.
steps.why: Typing the name forces a read of what is about to happen.

steps.title: Read the audit
steps.tell: Every call, allowed or blocked, is in the audit page with secrets redacted.
steps.say: I can show exactly what was asked, by whom, and what happened.
steps.why: A log of blocked calls is as useful as a log of allowed ones.

proof.happy: The write ran once, after the review, and the audit shows the call with its hash.
proof.blocked: The write was refused (writes off, or changed arguments), and the audit shows the refusal.

say: Nothing writes until someone has looked at exactly what it will write.
